title: Celigo ai-agent
description:
Configuration for an AI agent import. Set `aiAgent.provider` to choose
the LLM backend, then configure the matching format: `aiAgent.openai` for
OpenAI, `aiAgent.litellm` for Gemini and Anthropic Claude, or the generic
flat format (`aiAgent.model`, `aiAgent.modelOptions`, …) for the catalog
providers. Omit `_connectionId` to use platform-managed credentials on a
built-in provider; catalog providers need a BYOK connection to run.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
AI agents process structured records only. Do not send the import-level `blob` or
`blobKeyPath` fields — either one fails the save with 422 `not_supported`
("Field "blob" is not supported for this import type").

name.description: Display name for the AI agent.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server requires a non-empty name on create and caps its length, but accepts an empty name on update; the spec requires a non-empty name on every write.

description.description: Optional description of the AI agent's purpose.
examples: Classifies incoming support tickets by category and priority.

_connectionId.description:
Connection for BYOK (bring your own key) — an HTTP connection to the vendor's API.
Optional for the built-in providers (`openai`, `gemini`, `anthropic`), which run on
platform-managed credentials when it is omitted. Catalog providers (`mistral`, `xai`,
`huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`) have no platform-managed credentials: the agent
saves without one but cannot run until it is set.

_integrationId.description: Integration this AI agent belongs to. Omitted for a standalone agent.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Not nullable in the spec although the server stores an explicit null on a few agents; writers should send a real id or omit the field rather than null. This base is shared with the response, so validation deliberately flags those stored-null agents — intended steering toward the non-null shape, not an oversight.

x-enumDescriptions.AiAgentImport: AI agent import adaptor for LLM-powered data processing.

_connectorId.description: Connector this AI agent was created from, set when it is part of an installed integration app.

aiAgent.description:
AI Agent configuration used by both AiAgentImport and GuardrailImport (ai_agent type).

Configures which AI provider and model to use, along with instructions, parameter
tuning, output format, and available tools. Providers come in two families with
two configuration formats:

- **Built-in providers** — each has its own configuration block.
  - **openai**: OpenAI models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, etc.). Configure via the `openai` object.
  - **gemini**: Google Gemini models via the LiteLLM proxy. Configure via `litellm` with overrides in `litellm._overrides.gemini`.
  - **anthropic**: Anthropic Claude models via the LiteLLM proxy. Configure via `litellm` with overrides in `litellm._overrides.anthropic`.
- **Catalog providers** — `mistral`, `xai`, `huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`. Added
  as catalog data rather than platform code, they share one generic flat format:
  `model`, `modelOptions`, `instructions`, `output`, and the `tools` / `prompts` /
  `resources` arrays directly on this object.

A `_connectionId` on the parent import selects bring-your-own-key (BYOK)
credentials. Without one, built-in providers run on platform-managed
credentials; catalog providers have no platform-managed credentials, so they
save without a connection but cannot run until one is attached.

x-enumDescriptions.openai: Use OpenAI models via the OpenAI Responses API (built-in; `openai` block).
x-enumDescriptions.gemini: Use Google Gemini models via the LiteLLM proxy (built-in; `litellm` block).
x-enumDescriptions.anthropic: Use Anthropic Claude models via the LiteLLM proxy (built-in; `litellm` block).
x-enumDescriptions.mistral: Use Mistral models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).
x-enumDescriptions.xai: Use xAI Grok models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).
x-enumDescriptions.huggingface: Use Hugging Face inference endpoint models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).
x-enumDescriptions.deepseek: Use DeepSeek models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).
x-enumDescriptions.cohere: Use Cohere models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).
x-enumDescriptions.groq: Use Groq-hosted models (catalog provider; generic flat format, BYOK).

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server rejects any other value with `provider_not_found`; catalog providers are seeded as data, so new values can appear without a platform release — re-verify before adding one here.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The provider decides the configuration format, and the server rejects a
mismatch with 422 `invalid_provider_config_format`: `openai` needs the
`openai` block, `gemini` and `anthropic` need the `litellm` block (Gemini- or
Claude-specific settings under `litellm._overrides`), and the catalog
providers (`mistral`, `xai`, `huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`) need the
generic flat format — `model` and `modelOptions` directly on this object,
never an `openai` or `litellm` block.

Catalog providers are BYOK-only at run time: the agent saves without a
`_connectionId`, but its first run fails with 422 `invalid_request` ("No API
key configured for provider …"). Always attach an HTTP connection to the
vendor's API (token auth) when the provider is a catalog provider.

model.description:
Model identifier for a catalog provider (generic flat format) — for example
`grok-4.6`. Built-in providers set the model inside their own block
(`openai.model`, `litellm.model`) instead.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Open string by design — the catalog's model list changes without a spec release, and a BYOK connection passes any model string through to the vendor.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Required for every catalog provider — omitting it or sending an empty string
fails the save with 422 `missing_required_field`.

Without a `_connectionId` on the parent import the model must be one the
catalog lists for the provider: an unknown id fails the save with 422
`model_not_found`, a listed-but-disabled id with 422 `model_disabled`. With a
`_connectionId` (BYOK) any model string saves — the server does not check it
against the catalog or the vendor.

modelOptions.description:
Model tuning for a catalog provider (generic flat format). Which keys, values, and
ranges are accepted is defined per catalog model and validated on save when the
model is a catalog entry.

maxOutputTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model may generate.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth for models that expose it.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Bounds and the accepted key set differ per catalog model and are enforced by the server's per-model schema; encoding one model's limits here would be wrong for the next.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When the model is a catalog entry, the server validates this object against
that model's schema and fails the save with 422 `invalid_model_options`
naming the key: unknown keys are rejected, `reasoning_effort` must be one of
the enum values where the model accepts it at all (xAI's `grok-4.6` does;
DeepSeek's `deepseek-chat` rejects the key), and numeric bounds apply —
on `grok-4.6`, `temperature` ≤ 2, `topP` ≤ 1, `maxOutputTokens` ≥ 100.

With a `_connectionId` and a model the catalog does not list, the object is
passed through unvalidated — send only options the vendor's API accepts.

litellm.description:
LiteLLM proxy configuration. Used when `provider` is "gemini" or "anthropic".

LiteLLM provides a unified interface to multiple AI providers. Gemini-specific
settings are in `_overrides.gemini`; Claude-specific settings are in
`_overrides.anthropic`.

`model` is required when litellm is the active provider path.

model.description:
LiteLLM model identifier. For Gemini, models are stored without the `gemini/`
prefix; for Anthropic, use the Claude model id (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`).

x-celigo-ai-guidance:

import), the model must be one the platform hosts for the provider —
Gemini and Anthropic Claude both have a hosted list. The save does not

with 422 `invalid_model`, whose message lists the hosted models.

When `provider` is "anthropic", the value must be between 0 and 1 — a higher value

responseMapping.description:
Merges fields from a step's response back onto the in-flight record so
downstream steps can read them. Applies to both lookup steps
(`type: "export"`) and import steps (`type: "import"`); without it, the
step's response is discarded after the call.

`fields` and `lists` are plain arrays — exactly the shape GET returns.

Extract paths do NOT read the raw application response — the platform
wraps every response in a canonical per-record envelope first, and
extracts evaluate against that envelope:

- **Lookup steps**: `{"statusCode": 200, "data": [<result records>],
  "errors": []}` — `data` holds the records the lookup returned, so
  extracts must start from it: `data[0].name` copies a field of the
  first result, `data` copies the whole result array. A bare
  result-record field name (e.g. `name`) resolves to nothing and merges
  nothing.
- **Import steps**: `{"id": "<destination record id>", "statusCode": 200,
  "ignored": false, "errors": [], "_json": <raw destination response>}` —
  use `id` for the destination-assigned id and `_json.<path>` for fields
  inside the destination's response body. The full envelope (including
  `id`) is present on real runs and in flow-builder previews; flow TEST
  runs never execute imports, and their mock-built envelope carries no
  `id` — an `extract: "id"` merges nothing in a test run even though it
  works on real runs.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Send `fields` and `lists` as bare arrays, exactly as GET returns them.
Never wrap either in an object (e.g. `"fields": {"type": [...]}`): the
API does not reject that shape — it returns 200 and silently persists
`fields: [null]` / `lists: [{"fields": []}]`, erasing the step's
response mappings.

responseMapping is fully replaced on PUT: omitting it resets the step
to empty `{"fields": [], "lists": []}`. Always send the complete
intended mapping for every step.

To carry several lookup results onto the record, use `extract: "data"`
(the whole result array) or a `lists` entry whose extracts use
`data[*].x` — never `data[*].x` in `fields[].extract`, which merges
nothing: the record simply never gains the field.

fields.description:
Field mappings that copy individual values from the response
envelope onto the in-flight record.

extract.description:
Path within the canonical response envelope to copy the value
from. For lookup steps, paths start from the envelope's `data`
array (`data[0].x` and `data.0.x` are equivalent; `data` alone
copies every result); for import steps, use the envelope fields
`id`, `statusCode`, `ignored`, or `_json.<path>` for the raw
response body. Paths that skip the envelope (bare response
field names) resolve to nothing, and a `[*]` wildcard is not
honored here — `data[*].x` merges nothing; iterate arrays with
`lists` instead.

generate.description:
Field path on the in-flight record where the extracted value
is stored, using dot notation for nesting. Downstream steps
read the value at this path.

lists.description:
Array mappings that build a target array on the in-flight record
from an array inside the response envelope — one output item per
element of the array the item extracts mark with `[*]` (`data[*].x`
for lookups, `_json.<arrayPath>[*].x` for imports); an empty source
array yields an empty target array. Not needed for one-to-many
(fan-out) merge-back, which uses plain field mappings.

generate.description:
Array field created on the in-flight record to hold the
mapped items.

fields.description:
Field mappings applied to each item of the source array to
produce the corresponding target-array item.

extract.description:
Full envelope path to the source value, with `[*]`
marking the array to iterate — `data[*].productId` for a
lookup, `_json.items[*].sku` for an import. A path without
`[*]` (e.g. `statusCode`) repeats the same envelope value
on every item; an item-relative name (`productId`)
resolves to nothing and produces empty objects.

Selects the data context that `mappings[].extract` evaluates against. With no

filter.description:
Filter applied to incoming records before they are sent to the LLM. Records that match
continue through the agent; records that don't are silently dropped.

type.description:
Determines which filtering mechanism to use. This choice affects which properties
must be configured and how filtering logic is implemented.

**Available types**

**Rule-Based Filtering (`"expression"`)**
- **Required Config**: The `expression` object with rule definitions
- **Behavior**: Evaluates declarative rules against item attributes
- **Best For**: Common patterns like name matching, date ranges, value limits
- **Advantages**: Simpler to configure, no custom code required

**Script-Based Filtering (`"script"`)**
- **Required Config**: The `script` object with _scriptId and function
- **Behavior**: Executes custom JavaScript to determine which items to process
- **Best For**: Complex conditions, business logic, dynamic criteria
- **Advantages**: Maximum flexibility, can implement any logic

**Implementation guidance**

1. For standard filtering needs (name, size, date), use `"expression"`
2. For complex logic or conditions not covered by expressions, use `"script"`
3. When selecting a type, you must configure the corresponding object:
    - `type: "expression"` requires the `expression` object
    - `type: "script"` requires the `script` object

x-enumDescriptions.script: Script-based filtering using custom JavaScript logic.

expression.description:
Configuration for declarative rule-based filtering. This object enables filtering
items based on common attributes without requiring custom code.

**Usage context**

This object is REQUIRED when `filter.type` is set to "expression" and should not be
configured otherwise. It provides a standardized way to define filtering rules that
can match against item attributes like name, type, value, date, and other properties.

**Implementation guidance**

The expression system uses a rule-based approach where:
- Rules can be combined with AND/OR logic
- Each rule can check a specific attribute
- Multiple conditions can be applied (ranges, pattern matching, exact matches)

**Common filter patterns**

1. **Pattern matching**: Using wildcards like `*` and `?`
2. **Value range filtering**: Numbers between min and max values
3. **Date range filtering**: Items created/modified within specific time ranges
4. **Status checking**: Items with specific status values or properties

For AI agents: Rule-based filtering should be your first choice when the filtering criteria
can be expressed in terms of standard attributes. Only use script-based filtering when
more complex logic is required.

version.description:
Version identifier for the expression format. Currently only version "1" is supported.

This field ensures future compatibility if the expression format evolves. Always set to "1"
for current implementations.

x-enumDescriptions.1: Current and only supported filter expression version.

rules.description:
Expression array defining filter conditions using prefix notation. The first element is the operator,
followed by its operands which may themselves be nested expression arrays.

The rule expression follows this pattern:
- First element: Operator name (string)
- Remaining elements: Operands for that operator (values or nested expressions)

**Expression structure**

Filter expressions use a prefix notation where operators appear before their operands:
```
[operator, operand1, operand2, ...]
```

**Comparison Operators**
- `"equals"`: Exact match (equals)
- `"notequals"`: Not equal to value (not equals)
- `"greaterthan"`: Value is greater than specified value (is greater than)
- `"greaterthanequals"`: Value is greater than or equal to specified value (is greater than or equals)
- `"lessthan"`: Value is less than specified value (is less than)
- `"lessthanequals"`: Value is less than or equal to specified value (is less than or equals)
- `"startswith"`: String starts with specified prefix (starts with)
- `"endswith"`: String ends with specified suffix (ends with)
- `"contains"`: String contains specified substring (contains)
- `"doesnotcontain"`: String does not contain specified substring (does not contain)
- `"isempty"`: Field is empty or null (is empty)
- `"isnotempty"`: Field contains a value (is not empty)
- `"matches"`: Matches specified pattern (matches)

**Logical Operators**
- `"and"`: All conditions must be true
- `"or"`: At least one condition must be true
- `"not"`: Negates the condition

**Field Access and Type Conversion**
- `"extract"`: Access a field from the item by name
- `"settings"`: Access a custom setting from the flow, flow step, or integration configuration
- `"boolean"`: Convert value to Boolean type
- `"epochtime"`: Convert value to Epoch Time (Unix timestamp)
- `"number"`: Convert value to Number type
- `"string"`: Convert value to String type

**Field Access Details**

**Using `extract` to access record fields:**
- Retrieves values from the current record being processed
- Can access nested properties using dot notation (e.g., `"customer.email"`)
- Returns the raw field value which may need type conversion

**Using `settings` to access configuration values:**
- Retrieves values from the integration's configuration settings
- Supports different scopes with prefix notation:
  - `flow.settingName`: Access flow-level settings
  - `export.settingName`: Access export-level settings
  - `import.settingName`: Access import-level settings
  - `integration.settingName`: Access integration-level settings
- Useful for dynamic filtering based on configuration

**Field Transformations**
- `"lowercase"`: Convert string to lowercase
- `"uppercase"`: Convert string to uppercase
- `"ceiling"`: Round number up to the nearest integer
- `"floor"`: Round number down to the nearest integer
- `"abs"`: Get absolute value of a number

Type conversion operators are often necessary when comparing extracted field values against literals or when the field type doesn't match the comparison operator's expected type. For example:

```json
[
  "equals",
  [
    "number",  // Convert to number before comparison
    [
      "extract",
      "quantity"
    ]
  ],
  100
]
```

Example with datetime conversion:
```json
[
  "greaterthan",
  [
    "epochtime",  // Convert to Unix timestamp before comparison
    [
      "extract",
      "createdDate"
    ]
  ],
  1609459200000  // January 1, 2021 as Unix timestamp in milliseconds
]
```

Example with transformations:
```json
[
  "and",
  [
    "matches",
    [
      "lowercase",  // Convert to lowercase before matching
      [
        "string",
        [
          "extract",
          "categories"
        ]
      ]
    ],
    "netsuite"
  ],
  [
    "notequals",
    [
      "string",
      [
        "extract",
        "recurrence.pattern.type"
      ]
    ],
    ""
  ]
]
```

Example comparing a record field with a flow setting:
```json
[
  "equals",
  [
    "string",
    [
      "extract",
      "trantype"
    ]
  ],
  [
    "string",
    [
      "settings",
      "flow.trantype"
    ]
  ]
]
```

**Examples**

Example 1: Status field is not equal to "cancelled"
```json
[
  "notequals",
  [
    "extract",
    "status"
  ],
  "cancelled"
]
```

Example 2: Filename starts with "HC"
```json
[
  "startswith",
  [
    "extract",
    "filename"
  ],
  "HC"
]
```

Example 3: Amount is greater than 100
```json
[
  "greaterthan",
  [
    "number",
    [
      "extract",
      "amount"
    ]
  ],
  100
]
```

Example 4: Order date is after January 1, 2023
```json
[
  "greaterthan",
  [
    "extract",
    "orderDate"
  ],
  "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"
]
```

Example 5: Category contains any of ["Urgent", "High Priority"]
```json
[
  "anyof",
  [
    "extract",
    "category"
  ],
  ["Urgent", "High Priority"]
]
```

script.description:
Configuration for programmable script-based filtering. This object enables complex, custom
filtering logic beyond what expression-based filtering can provide.

**Usage context**

This object is REQUIRED when `filter.type` is set to "script" and should not be configured
otherwise. It provides a way to execute custom JavaScript code to determine which items
should be processed.

**Implementation approach**

Script-based filtering works by:
1. Executing the specified function from the referenced script
2. Passing item data to the function
3. Using the function's return value (true/false) to determine inclusion

**Common use cases**

Script filtering is ideal for:
- Complex business logic that can't be expressed as simple rules
- Dynamic filtering criteria that change based on external factors
- Content-based filtering that requires deep inspection
- Advanced pattern matching beyond simple wildcards
- Multi-stage filtering with intermediate logic

For AI agents: Only use script-based filtering when expression-based filtering is insufficient.
Script filtering requires maintaining custom code, which adds complexity to the integration.

_scriptId.description:
Reference to the Script resource that contains the filtering logic. This must be a valid
ObjectId of a Script resource that exists in the system.

The referenced script must contain the function specified in the `function` field
and must be written to handle filtering specifically. The script receives
item data as its input and must return a boolean value indicating whether
to process the item (true) or skip it (false).

Format: 24-character hexadecimal string (MongoDB ObjectId)

function.description:
Name of the function within the script to execute for filtering decisions. This function
must exist in the script referenced by _scriptId.

**Function requirements**

The specified function must:
- Accept item data as its first parameter
- Return a boolean value (true to process the item, false to skip it)
- Handle errors gracefully
- Execute efficiently (as it may run for many items)

**Function signature**

```javascript
function filterItems(itemData) {
  // itemData contains properties of the item being evaluated
  // Custom logic here
  return true; // or false to skip the item
}
```

For AI agents: Ensure the function name exactly matches a function defined in the
referenced script, as mismatches will cause the filter to fail.

responseTransform.description:
Transformation that reshapes the LLM's response after records are processed, before the
response is handled by response mappings and downstream steps.

type.description:
Determines which transformation mechanism to use. This choice affects which properties
must be configured and how transformation logic is implemented.

**Available types**

**Rule-Based Transformation (`"expression"`)**
- **Required Config**: The `expression` object with mapping definitions
- **Behavior**: Applies declarative rules to reshape data
- **Best For**: Most transformation scenarios from simple to complex
- **Advantages**: Visual configuration, no coding required

**Script-Based Transformation (`"script"`)**
- **Required Config**: The `script` object with _scriptId and function
- **Behavior**: Executes custom JavaScript to transform data
- **Best For**: Extremely complex logic or proprietary algorithms
- **Advantages**: Maximum flexibility, can implement any logic

**Implementation guidance**

1. For standard data transformations, use `"expression"`
2. For complex logic or specialized processing, use `"script"`
3. When selecting a type, you must configure the corresponding object:
    - `type: "expression"` requires the `expression` object
    - `type: "script"` requires the `script` object

x-enumDescriptions.expression: Rule-based transformation using declarative mapping definitions.
x-enumDescriptions.script: Script-based transformation using custom JavaScript logic.

expression.description:
Configuration for declarative rule-based transformations. This object enables reshaping data
without requiring custom code.

**Usage context**

This object is REQUIRED when `transform.type` is set to "expression" and should not be
configured otherwise. It provides a standardized way to define transformation rules that
can map, modify, and generate data elements.

**Implementation guidance**

The expression system uses a rule-based approach where:
- Field mappings define how input data is transformed to target fields
- Formulas can be used to calculate or generate new values
- Lookups can enrich data by fetching related information
- Mode determines how records are processed (create new or modify existing)

version.description:
Version of the expression format. Determines which rules
property contains the transformation logic.

x-enumDescriptions.1: Legacy format. Rules are in the `rules` array (array of arrays of extract/generate objects).
x-enumDescriptions.2: Current format. Rules are in the `rulesTwoDotZero` object with mode, mappings, and lookups.

rules.description:
Transformation rules for version 1 expressions. An array of
rule groups; each group is an array of field-mapping objects.
Most transforms have a single group. Present when `version`
is `"1"`. The output record contains ONLY the generated
fields — every unmapped field is dropped (v1 has no
equivalent of Transform 2.0's `modify` mode), and the
record's trace key does not survive the rebuild.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
v1 rules REPLACE the record: a one-field rule group drops
every other field, silently breaking downstream filters,
router branch rules, and templates that referenced the
dropped fields. Either map every field downstream logic
needs forward, or author Transform 2.0 with
``mode: "modify"`` instead.

extract.description:
Source field path to read from. Supports multiple
syntaxes: bare field names (`id`), dot notation
(`fulfillment.shipment_id`), slash-prefixed paths
for XML (`/FeedProcessingStatus`), wildcards (`*.id`,
`*.[Internal ID]`), and array indexing (`SDF[0]`).

generate.description:
Target field name to write to. Typically a bare name
(`id`) or dot path (`SDF.Filter.ID`).

key.description:
Auto-generated identifier for this rule, used by the
UI to track individual rules for editing and reordering.

rulesTwoDotZero.description:
Configuration for version 2 transformation rules. This object contains the core logic
for how data is mapped, enriched, and transformed.

**Capabilities**

Transformation 2.0 provides:
- Precise field mapping with JSONPath expressions
- Support for deeply nested data structures
- Formula-based field generation
- Dynamic lookups for data enrichment
- Multiple operating modes to fit different scenarios

mode.description:
Transformation mode that determines how records are handled during processing.

**Available modes**

**Create Mode (`"create"`)**
- **Behavior**: Builds entirely new output records from inputs
- **Use When**: Output structure differs significantly from input
- **Advantage**: Clean slate approach, no field inheritance

**Modify Mode (`"modify"`)**
- **Behavior**: Makes targeted edits to existing records
- **Use When**: Output structure should remain similar to input
- **Advantage**: Preserves unmapped fields from the original record

x-enumDescriptions.create: Builds entirely new output records from inputs, ignoring unmapped fields.
x-enumDescriptions.modify: Makes targeted edits to existing records, preserving unmapped fields.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
On a grouped record (the export groups rows, so the record is an
array) only `create` can author output — build it from the rows with
`$[0].field`, `$[*].field`, or a `buildArrayHelper` over `$[*]`.
`modify` has no object to overlay onto an array: the record passes
through untouched and the processor reports success. Either mode
reshapes the inside of one record; neither changes how many records
the page carries (that is the export's `preSavePage` hook) or whether
the export groups at all (that is its grouping setting).

x-enumDescriptions.record: The transform processor evaluates `mappings[].extract` JSONPath against the flat record itself (`$.field`, no `record.` segment) — the default when absent.
x-enumDescriptions.envelope: The transform processor evaluates JSONPath against the wrapped runtime envelope `{record, settings, job, …}` (file-provider steps also carry `fileMeta`) — extracts must include the `record.` segment (`$.record.field`).

inputContext.description:
Controls the JSON shape the transformTwoDotZero processor
evaluates `mappings[].extract` JSONPath values against at
flow runtime. Applies only to Transform 2.0 (v2,
`rulesTwoDotZero`); v1 transforms (the `rules` array on
`transform.expression.rules`) and script-mode transforms
ignore this field.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
## Extract anchoring by mode

- `record` (default — absent / empty / undefined): the
  processor sees the FLAT record as its evaluation root.
  `mappings[].extract` JSONPath MUST anchor directly at
  `$` with NO `record.` segment — e.g. `"$.orderId"`,
  `"$.customer.email"`; PLACEHOLDER extracts use
  `"$.PLACEHOLDER_<field>"`.
  This is the dominant Celigo idiom and the right choice for new transforms.
- `envelope`: the processor sees a wrapped object
  `{record: {...}, settings: ..., job: ...}` (plus
  `fileMeta` on file-provider steps).
  `mappings[].extract` JSONPath MUST include the
  `record.` segment — e.g. `"$.record.orderId"`;
  PLACEHOLDER extracts use `"$.record.PLACEHOLDER_<field>"`.
  Pick this only when the transform was authored against
  the envelope shape on purpose.

Handlebars expressions inside `extract`
(`{{record.field}}`, `{{dateFormat ... record.field}}`)
ALWAYS reference the `record` root regardless of
`inputContext` — only JSONPath anchoring flips.

Emit `inputContext` explicitly on new v2 transforms:
unset is read as `record`, but stating it makes the
extract-anchoring contract self-documenting and immune
to a platform default change.

## Allowed values

- ``record`` (default — emitted when the field is absent
  / empty / undefined): the transform processor sees
  the FLAT record itself as its evaluation root.
  ``mappings[].extract`` JSONPath values MUST anchor
  directly at ``$`` with NO ``record.`` segment — for
  example ``"$.orderId"`` or
  ``"$.customer.email"``.  PLACEHOLDER extracts use
  ``"$.PLACEHOLDER_<field>"``.  This is the dominant
  Celigo idiom and the right choice for new transforms.

- ``envelope``: the transform processor sees a wrapped
  object of the shape
  ``{record: {...}, settings: ..., job: ...}`` (plus
  ``fileMeta`` on file-provider steps) — the
  same runtime-context envelope Handlebars / SQL /
  GraphQL specialists consume.  ``mappings[].extract``
  JSONPath values MUST include the ``record.`` segment
  — for example ``"$.record.orderId"`` or
  ``"$.record.customer.email"``.  PLACEHOLDER extracts
  use ``"$.record.PLACEHOLDER_<field>"``.  Pick this
  mode only when the export was authored against the
  envelope shape on purpose (typically because an
  upstream step intentionally feeds the wrapped
  runtime context through to the transform).

## Handlebars expressions are NOT affected

Handlebars expressions inside ``extract``
(``{{record.field}}``,
``{{dateFormat ... record.field}}``, etc.) ALWAYS
reference the runtime context's ``record`` root
regardless of ``inputContext`` — the Handlebars runtime
always sees the wrapped envelope.  Only JSONPath
behavior flips with this field.

## Agent guidance

Set this field explicitly on every new v2 transform
the agent authors.  Leaving it unset is interpreted as
``record`` by the platform, but emitting
``inputContext: record`` makes the contract
self-documenting and prevents the transform from
drifting into envelope mode if an upstream change ever
changes the platform default.  The TransformsAgent
reads this value off the transform config and threads
it into the generator's prompt so the JSONPath form
matches the runtime root.

## fileMeta on file-provider steps

File-provider exports and lookups populate a
``fileMeta`` envelope key describing each record's
source file: ``fileName``, ``fileSize``, and
``lastModifiedTime`` (epoch milliseconds).  Reach it
as ``$.fileMeta.<field>`` in envelope mode, or as
``{{fileMeta.<field>}}`` from a Handlebars extract in
either mode.  The keys are exactly these three —
lowercase variants such as ``filesize`` or
``filename`` resolve empty.  The standalone transform
processor substitutes sample fileMeta values when the
posted data lacks them, so a resolving editor render
is not proof the step provides fileMeta — only
file-provider steps populate it at flow runtime.

script.description:
Configuration for programmable script-based transformations. This object enables complex, custom
transformation logic beyond what expression-based transformations can provide.

**Usage context**

This object is REQUIRED when `transform.type` is set to "script" and should not be configured
otherwise. It provides a way to execute custom JavaScript code to transform data according to
specialized business rules or complex algorithms.

**Implementation approach**

Script-based transformation works by:
1. Executing the specified function from the referenced script
2. Passing input data to the function
3. Using the function's return value as the transformed output

**Common use cases**

Script transformation is ideal for:
- Complex business logic that can't be expressed through mappings
- Algorithmic transformations requiring computation
- Dynamic transformations based on external factors
- Legacy system data format compatibility
- Multi-stage processing with intermediate steps

Only use script-based transformation when expression-based transformation is insufficient.
Script transformation requires maintaining custom code, which adds complexity to the integration.

_scriptId.description:
Reference to a predefined script resource containing the transformation logic.

The referenced script should contain the function specified in the
'function' property.

function.description:
Name of the function within the script to execute for transformation. This function
must exist in the script referenced by _scriptId.

hooks.description:
Custom JavaScript hooks that run at fixed points in the agent's import lifecycle.
AI agents do not aggregate records, so the `postAggregate` hook that other import
types expose is intentionally omitted here.

preMap.description: Hook that runs on each page of records before the agent's mappings are applied.

function.description: Function to invoke within the referenced script.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Do not require function alongside _scriptId — the server accepts function-less hook stubs on write.

_scriptId.description: Script containing the hook function named in `function`.

_stackId.description: Stack that hosts the hook logic, used instead of a script for stack-based deployments.

configuration.description:
Static parameters passed to the hook function at runtime, letting one script be
reused with different settings. Null when the hook carries no static parameters.

postMap.description: Hook that runs after mappings are applied, before records are sent to the LLM.

postSubmit.description: Hook that runs after the LLM responds, with both the submitted records and the responses.

oneToMany.description:
When true, the step runs once per child record instead of once per incoming record.
`pathToMany` names the array field that holds the children inside an object record; when
the incoming record is itself an array (grouped or row-based data), leave `pathToMany` blank
and each element becomes a record. The fan-out is scoped to this step: afterwards the children
are re-joined into the record's original shape — the object with its array, or the array of rows —
carrying any response-mapping enrichment, and that re-joined record is what the next step
receives. Not for locating records in an export's HTTP response; use
`http.response.resourcePath` for that. Applies to steps that receive a record — imports and
lookups (an export referenced as a page processor of a flow, API, or Tool). A standalone export
(a flow's page generator) has no incoming record, so the fields are saved but have no effect on
the records it produces; to emit one record per array element from a standalone export, use a
`hooks.preSavePage` script, or for a file-definition export make the repeating segment the
record boundary in the definition's rules.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Only imports and lookups (exports placed as page processors) fan out. On a standalone export
(a flow's page generator) the API saves ``oneToMany`` / ``pathToMany`` and applies neither:
the records reach the next step unchanged and no error is raised. Live-verified 2026-09-18 on
a flow test run — an order record with three ``lines`` reached the import as ONE record with
the setting on the export, and as THREE child records with the same setting on the import.
Never propose these fields as the way to split a standalone export's records; that is
``hooks.preSavePage`` work (or, for a file definition, the definition's record boundary).
The rules below apply only on a step that receives a record.

Two modes, decided by the SHAPE of the record entering the step. Object record with a child
array under a field → set ``pathToMany`` to that field. Array record (a ``groupByFields``
export, a CSV/file group, a script that returns an array) → leave ``pathToMany`` blank; each
element becomes one record. Live-verified 2026-09-10 on flows, Tools, and APIs.

Blank ``pathToMany`` on an OBJECT record fails every record with code ``oneToMany_error``:
"Failed to extract child records from oneToMany import data. Record at index 0 was not an
array, and no PathToMany was provided". Builder previews return only the code, with no
message. The fix is never "turn oneToMany off" by default — first determine whether the
record arriving at the step is an object (set a path) or an array (blank is correct; a
preview error on an array-fed step is the preview panel re-applying one-to-many to the
already-fanned-out record — verify with a test run or a real run).

Child record shape differs by mode. Path mode: each child is the array element plus
``_PARENT`` (the parent record minus the array). Blank/row mode: each child is the element
itself, with no ``_PARENT``. In both modes templates on the step reference the child as
``{{record.<field>}}``; a response mapping on a one-to-many lookup merges into each child and
the downstream step receives the re-joined parent (path mode) or the re-joined array (row
mode) with every element enriched.

One-to-many never batches by itself: ``batch_of_records`` appears as the HTTP body template
root only when ``http.batchSize`` is greater than 1 (children are batched after fan-out).
With the default batch size the template root is ``record``.

pathToMany.description:
Path to the array of child records inside an object record when `oneToMany` is true, in dot
notation (`items`, `lines.lineItems`). Leave blank when the incoming record is itself an array
(grouped or row-based data) — each element is then a child record. A path that does not resolve
to an array processes zero records and reports success. Read only on steps that receive a
record (imports, lookup exports); on a standalone export it is saved and ignored — see `oneToMany`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Inert on a standalone export (a flow's page generator) exactly like ``oneToMany`` — the value
is saved, the export's records reach the next step unchanged, and nothing errors
(live-verified 2026-09-18). Splitting a standalone export's records into one per element is
``hooks.preSavePage`` work, or the file definition's record boundary; never this field.

Set this ONLY when the record entering the step is an object whose children sit under a field.
On an array record (a ``groupByFields`` export, a CSV/file group, a script returning an array)
any path resolves to nothing: the step processes ZERO children, builds no request, and reports
success with no error. Live-verified 2026-09-10 — the failure is silent, so confirm the arriving
record's shape (test run stage data, or the flow builder's input panel: ``rows`` means array).

Blank with an object record is the ``oneToMany_error`` failure ("Record at index 0 was not an
array, and no PathToMany was provided"); blank with an array record is the correct row-based
configuration. An empty string behaves exactly like an absent field.

Use the bare field name or dotted path (``lineItems``, ``details.items``), not a JSONPath
expression. Each child in path mode carries ``_PARENT`` (the parent minus the array), so
parent-level fields are read as ``{{record._PARENT.<field>}}``.

distributed.description: Always false for AI agent imports — the agent executes on Celigo's servers, not inside a target application.

maxAttempts.description: Maximum number of attempts made to deliver a record before it is marked as failed.

ignoreExisting.description: When true, records that already exist in the destination are silently skipped. Rarely meaningful for AI agents; accepted for import-surface parity.

ignoreMissing.description: When true, records that do not already exist in the destination are silently skipped. Rarely meaningful for AI agents; accepted for import-surface parity.

blob.description:
AI agents process structured records only. `true` (and any `blobKeyPath`) fails the
save with 422 `not_supported`; an explicit `false` is accepted and echoed back, which
is the only way the field appears on the wire.

mockResponse.description:
Predefined response records used in place of calling the LLM when testing the agent,
so flows can run without spending tokens. Records must be in integrator.io canonical
format — the server rejects any other shape with a 422.

statusCode.description: HTTP status code the mock returns (e.g. 200, 403).

id.description: Identifier echoed for the mocked record.

ignored.description: When true, the mocked record reports as ignored rather than imported.

dataURI.description: Data URI echoed for the mocked record.

errors.description: Mock error entries returned with the record.

_json.description: Mock response body for structured-output agents.

_text.description: Mock response body for text-output agents.

blobKey.description:
Part of the generic import mock-response format and echoed back if sent, but
never produced by an AI agent — agents cannot run in blob mode (`blob: true`
is rejected). Omit it.
